title: quantization-nan-debug-breadcrumbs-maya-2026-03-28
content:
Purpose:
- Personal scratchpad for the NaN/quality incidents observed after switching Llama-3-small->int8 and fp8 tests last week. Keeping a timeline, commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses and next steps so Lee/Jordan can pick up.

Summary of the problem:
- Intermittent NaNs (or catastrophic quality drop) observed during inference on int8 and fp8 quantized variants. BF16 seems mostly stable.
- Symptoms: sometimes a token becomes <nan> in logits and then generation collapses; other times model returns gibberish (repeated tokens) after ~80 tokens. Not deterministic but higher frequency when batch size >1 or with KV cache enabled.
- Repro rate: ~20-40% on my local perf box (A100-40GB) when using our int8 kernel; ~5-10% for fp8 path. BF16 path ~0-1%.

Environment:
- Model: redwood/llama3-small-like (internal variant), sequence length 2048 default.
- Serving runtime: local dev build of serving-runtime @ commit 8f3c9a (kernel selection changes).
- PyTorch: 2.2.1+cu122 (build used by runtime).
- bitsandbytes: 0.40.0 (custom patched for fp8 support).
- CUDA: 12.2
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04, Drivers 535.xx

Commands / reproducer attempts (local):
1) Minimal single-process repro (int8 path):
   python reproduce_infer.py --model redwood/llama3-small --quantize int8 --batch 4 --prefill 64 --generate 128 --use-kv-cache True --seed 42
   - Observed: NaN logits at token 93, generation aborted.

2) Compare BF16 vs INT8:
   python reproduce_infer.py --model redwood/llama3-small --quantize bf16 --batch 4 --prefill 64 --generate 128 --use-kv-cache True --seed 42
   - Observed: BF16 completes fine, outputs coherent continuation.

3) FP8 run (custom bnb FP8 kernel):
   python reproduce_infer.py --model redwood/llama3-small --quantize fp8 --batch 4 --prefill 64 --generate 128 --use-kv-cache True --seed 42
   - Observed: occasional NaN at token ~105; less frequent than int8 but present.

4) Disable KV cache:
   python reproduce_infer.py ... --use-kv-cache False
   - Observed: failure rate drops significantly for int8 (from ~30% to ~5%). Suggests KV cache interaction.

Representative error snippets / logs:
- Log extract from int8 run: 
  [2026-03-25 11:23:12] ERROR serving-runtime: Detected non-finite logits [nan, nan, ...] at layer 17 head 3.
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "runtime/generate.py", line 312, in generate_loop
      logits = step(model_state)
    File "runtime/engine.py", line 198, in step
      attn_out = cuda_kernel_attention(q,k,v,...)
  RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered

- Python-level detection (post-hoc):
  if not torch.isfinite(logits).all():
      logger.error(f"Non-finite logits at step {step_idx} - {logits[:8]}")

What I've ruled out so far:
- Not a random seed-only fluke: reproducible with same seed ~20% of runs.
- Not purely out-of-memory: no OOM, CUDA memstats stable.
- Not a tokenization bug: same tokens with bf16.
- Not a specific prompt (seen across multiple prompts).

Initial hypotheses:
1) Quantization kernel numerical instability in attention or layernorm when merged with KV cache (accumulated rounding error leads to extreme values).
2) A bug in our custom FP8/INT8 GEMM kernel when sequence length > cached length or when reusing KV cache buffers (race/overwrite).
3) Improper scale management for FP8 path (scale update delayed or mis-applied causing overflow).
4) Broken dequantize path for residual accumulation (int8 dequantizing into float32 with incorrect scale).
5) CUDA kernel launches with wrong grid/block when batch>1 leading to memory corruption (explains higher freq with batch>1).

Quick local experiments (results):
- Forcing single-threaded CUDA launches (no streams): reduced failure rate but not eliminated.
- Running with smaller batch size (1) almost eliminates issue.
- Running with disabled fused layernorm (fallback to fnorm) eliminated NaNs in one trial — suspicious for fused kernel.
- Enabling strict fp32 accumulation (force accumulation dtype=float32) reduces failure rate.

Detailed reproducer notes:
- Minimal reproducer script uses timestep-by-timestep generation to catch first NaN:
  - load model with quantization flags (bnb or internal quantizer)
  - run forward token-by-token, after each token check torch.isfinite on logits, kv cache tensors, attention scores
  - dump offending tensors to /tmp/nan-dump-<timestamp>.npz (I started dumping q,k,v for layer 16/17 and attention scores).
- Example dump shows attention scores with huge exponents (exp(large) -> inf) causing softmax -> NaN in some runs.

Binary search plan to bisect change:
- Bisect recent commits in serving-runtime that touched kernel selection and KV cache reuse (range commit 7a2..8f3).
- Run repro 10x per commit on local A100, track failures.

What to inspect next (concrete steps):
1) Re-run repro with ASAN/UBSAN for CUDA if possible (we recently enabled some sanitizers in debug images) to catch memory corruption.
2) Add per-kernel checksum for KV cache buffers after writes to detect overwrites. Quick patch added locally (write uint64 hash) — will run overnight.
3) Reproduce with different driver (535.x vs 535.y) to rule out driver-specific issues.
4) Re-run with fused layernorm disabled globally to see if that isolates the problem to fused kernels.
5) Instrument bnb fp8 scale update path: log scales per-layer per-step to ensure scale not hitting 0 or inf.
6) Try small model (2-layer) to see if it scales with depth. If small model stable -> scale/accumulation error likely depth-cumulative.

Notes for Lee/Jordan (what I think):
- My money is on either (a) a kernel bug in fused attention / KV reuse causing memory corruption that manifests as NaNs, or (b) an FP8 scale update bug that occasionally sets an invalid scale leading to overflow. BF16 path avoids these code paths, hence stability. The fact disabling KV cache and fused layernorm reduces frequency strongly points to kernel-level issues.

Quick patches tried (and results):
- Force accumulate in fp32 (patch in engine to cast accumulators to float32): failure rate drops from 30%->3%.
- Disable fused layernorm: failure drops to ~2-4%.
- Add per-layer scale clamp on FP8 path (min 1e-8 max 1e8): inconsistent effect, reduces some crashes but not all.

Immediate next runs I will start (overnight):
- Bisect CI run across commits 7a2..8f3 (10x each)
- Run kernel checksum instrument overnight (will produce dumps if mismatch)
- Run small-model targeted test with heavy batch (batch 8) to try to trigger quickly

Longer-term plan:
- If bisect points to our kernel changes, we should revert the offending commit and open small hotfix PR that disables kernel by default until we audit it.
- If it is an FP8 scale management issue, we should add more robust scale clamping and explicit per-step validation, plus integration tests that exercise extreme token sequences.

Helpful artifacts I produced (in this drive):
- /users/maya/quantization-nan-dump-2026-03-25.npz (zipped tensor dumps from one failing run)
- Reproducer: /users/maya/reproduce_infer.py
- Patch branch: GH PR 432 (instrumentation and clamp changes)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is there any test infra we can run with ASAN for our CUDA kernels in CI? (ask infra/release-eng)
- Can Lee try the reproducer on a V100 and a 80GB A100 to see if memory foot-print changes alter behavior?
- Should we add nightly fuzz runs across quantization modes to catch regressions earlier?

If you're reading this and pick it up: start with reproducer + disable fused layernorm + run with batch 4 x 10 seeds to get baseline. I will leave my instrumented branch checked out on my laptop (branch: debug/quant-nan-march).

Logs / attachments: see linked_artifacts and files in /users/maya/ in Drive.

-- Maya
